changes.after: Make a profile card fit a small space and stop growing in a large one.

before: A responsive card fits the space available instead of assuming every screen is wide. Responsive means adapting to different sizes. A width sets the requested width; max-width caps how large it can become. width: 100% asks for the available width of its containing block, usually its parent here. max-width: 360px stops the card growing beyond 360 CSS pixels. Together they can produce a narrow card on a small screen and a capped card on a large screen. The content, padding, and border still need to fit that width.

With the default content-box sizing, a declared width measures only the content. Padding and borders add extra width outside that measurement. A 300px content width with 12px padding on each side and 2px borders uses 328px in total. border-box includes padding and border in the declared width, so that same declared 300px includes them. Margin remains outside the box in either case. width: 100% plus border-box is useful here because padding will not make the card wider than its parent's available width. Long unbroken content can still overflow, so test the actual content too.

A percentage is a share of a reference size. In this card example, width percentages refer to the containing block's width. 75% of 400px is 0.75 × 400px, or 300px. 60% of 500px is 300px. 100% is the whole available share. A cap can reduce the final size: 100% of a 600px parent asks for 600px, but max-width: 360px stops at 360px. These values describe the CSS box; box-sizing determines whether its padding and border are included. The parent's padding may also affect the available width.

This HTML fragment belongs inside body and works with the previous CSS. Supply a real painter.jpg image file. ```html
Creative

Morgan

I like trying new colors and making small sketches.

``` article groups the profile, span wraps the short badge, and img provides the picture and its text replacement. max-width: 100% keeps the image from exceeding the card's content width. height: auto preserves its aspect ratio, the relationship between width and height. display: block makes the image use a block layout instead of sitting on a text baseline.

A badge often needs a small box that can sit beside text. display: inline-block lets it remain in an inline flow while accepting padding and box dimensions. border-radius rounds its corners; it does not change its meaning. Test the card with a longer description, a large image, and a narrower preview. Horizontal overflow means content sticks past the available width and may cause sideways scrolling. A width cap alone does not prevent overflow from every possible child, so inspect both the card and its contents at the supplied widths.

For the supplied profile, use .card with width: 100%, a positive max-width, border-box sizing, and automatic side margins. Constrain .card img with max-width: 100% and height: auto. Keep the badge and description inside the card on narrow screens. The checks confirm a width cap, the percentage image constraint, border-box sizing, and the supplied local image’s fit and 2:1 aspect ratio. They do not measure every possible overflow case. Resize the preview and watch the actual edges. Explain why width and max-width do different jobs, and calculate a percentage width before trying a different percentage.
after: Responsive means adjusting to the space available. `width: 100%` asks a card to fill its parent’s available width. `max-width` sets a limit so the card does not keep growing on a wide screen.

`box-sizing` chooses what a stated width includes. With `content-box`, padding and borders add to the content width. A 300-pixel content area, 12 pixels of padding on each side, and 2-pixel borders use 328 pixels altogether. With `border-box`, the stated 300 pixels already includes padding and borders. Margin stays outside in both cases.

A percentage means a share of another size. For this card, the reference is its parent’s available width. Half of 360 pixels is 180 pixels, so `width: 50%` asks for 180 pixels. A `max-width` can limit the result further.

Resize the preview and look at the card’s edges. Overflow means content sticks outside the available space. A card’s width limit does not stop every long word or large child from overflowing. Keep the supplied image’s shape, and check that the badge and description stay inside.
